title: 142. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Area and Volume Scaling Under Length Changes
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the area multiplier when the side length of a square is doubled.
questions.question: A square has side length \(s\). If the side length is doubled to \(2s\), by what factor does the area increase?
questions.explanation: The original area is \(s^2\). The new area is \((2s)^2=4s^2\). Therefore, the area increases by a factor of \(\frac{4s^2}{s^2}=4\). Option B is the length factor, not the area factor.
questions.hint: Identify whether the requested quantity is a length, an area, or a volume.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the volume multiplier when the edge length of a cube is tripled.
questions.question: A cube has edge length \(s\). If each edge is tripled to \(3s\), by what factor does the volume increase?
questions.explanation: The original volume is \(s^3\). The new volume is \((3s)^3=27s^3\). Therefore, the volume increases by a factor of \(27\). Option A is the area factor, not the volume factor.
questions.hint: Count how many length factors define the requested quantity.

questions.concept: Area Scaling for Rectangles Under Two-Dimensional Scaling
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area multiplier when both dimensions of a rectangle are multiplied by \(3\).
questions.question: A rectangle has length \(L\) and width \(W\). Both the length and the width are multiplied by \(3\). By what factor does the area increase?
questions.explanation: The original area is \(LW\). The new area is \((3L)(3W)=9LW\). Therefore, the area increases by a factor of \(9\). Option B incorrectly adds the two scale factors instead of multiplying them.
questions.hint: Multiply the two scaled dimensions and compare the product with the original area.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the area multiplier from a given positive circle-radius scale factor.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(r\). If the radius is multiplied by \(5\), giving radius \(5r\), by what factor does its area increase?
questions.explanation: Circle area is proportional to the square of its radius. The area factor is \(5^2=25\). The alternative \(5\) applies the length factor directly to an area.
questions.hint: Identify whether the requested quantity is a length, an area, or a volume.

questions.concept: Volume Scaling from a Given Initial Volume
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the new volume when the edge lengths of a cube are doubled.
questions.question: A cube has volume \(8\text{ cm}^3\). If each edge is doubled, what is the new volume?
questions.explanation: Doubling each edge multiplies volume by \(2^3=8\). Therefore, the new volume is \(8\times 8=64\text{ cm}^3\). Option A incorrectly doubles the volume instead of multiplying by \(8\).
questions.hint: Count how many length factors define the requested quantity.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the area ratio of two similar rectangles from their corresponding side ratio.
questions.question: Two similar rectangles have corresponding sides in the ratio \(2:5\). What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: For similar figures, the area ratio is the square of the corresponding length ratio. Here, \(\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^2=\frac{4}{25}\), so the area ratio is \(4:25\). Option B is the length ratio, not the area ratio.
questions.hint: Area depends on two length dimensions, so apply the length ratio twice.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the volume ratio of two similar solids from their corresponding length ratio.
questions.question: Two similar solids have corresponding lengths in the ratio \(2:3\). What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.explanation: For similar solids, the volume ratio is the cube of the corresponding length ratio. Here, \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3=\frac{8}{27}\), so the volume ratio is \(8:27\). Option A is the surface area ratio, not the volume ratio.
questions.hint: Identify whether the requested quantity is a length, an area, or a volume.

questions.concept: Length Scale Factor from Volume Scale Factor
questions.learningObjective: Determine the length scale factor when the volume scale factor is known.
questions.question: A solid is enlarged so that its volume is multiplied by \(64\). By what factor are all corresponding lengths multiplied?
questions.explanation: If all lengths are multiplied by \(k\), the volume is multiplied by \(k^3\). We need \(k^3=64\), so \(k=\sqrt[3]{64}=4\). Therefore, all corresponding lengths are multiplied by \(4\). Option A is the square root, not the cube root.
questions.hint: Volume is multiplied by the cube of the length scale factor; work backwards from the volume factor.

questions.concept: Surface Area Scaling for Rectangular Prisms
questions.learningObjective: Determine the surface area multiplier from a given common prism-length scale factor.
questions.question: A rectangular prism has dimensions \(2\text{ cm}\), \(3\text{ cm}\), and \(4\text{ cm}\). All corresponding lengths are multiplied by \(4\). By what factor does the surface area change?
questions.explanation: Every surface face has two length factors, so its area and the total surface area are multiplied by \(4^2=16\). The alternative \(64\) uses the volume factor \(4^3\) instead.
questions.hint: Each face area is a product of two lengths, so decide how many times the scale factor applies.

questions.concept: Volume Ratio from Surface Area Ratio of Similar Solids
questions.learningObjective: Determine the volume ratio of two similar cones from their surface area ratio.
questions.question: Two similar cones have surface areas in the ratio \(9:16\). What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.explanation: The corresponding length ratio is \(\sqrt{9}:\sqrt{16}=3:4\). Cube the length ratio to obtain the volume ratio \(3^3:4^3=27:64\). The alternative \(9:16\) reuses the area ratio without converting it to a volume ratio.
questions.hint: Identify whether the requested quantity is a length, an area, or a volume.
